title: Rainbow Looks for Friends
summary: Rainbow is a fish of every colour, and so shy that he spends all day hiding in his coral. Until along comes an octopus who knows how to wait.

scenes.text:
Deep, deep down in the sea, where the water is blue and cool, lived a little fish called Rainbow.

He was named after his scales. His tail was red, his tummy orange, his back yellow, his fins green and his head blue and violet.

When a ray of sunlight reached all the way down and touched his scales, the water filled with sparkles.

But Rainbow was very, very shy.

When other fish swam past, playing and laughing, he hid in his coral and kept very still, hardly breathing. He was scared to talk. He was scared to play. He was scared they would make fun of him.

So he spent his days alone, counting bubbles.

One morning, a lilac octopus stopped right in front of his coral.

He had two goggly eyes and a lopsided smile.

"Hello, hello, hello!" he said, waving all eight arms at once.

Rainbow squeezed further into the coral.

The octopus didn't come any closer. He didn't push. He just floated there calmly, waiting.

"My name's Lolo," he said after a while. "I saw your colours from far away. You look like a rainbow under the water."

Rainbow peeped out with one eye.

"Do you want to play hide-and-seek?" asked Lolo. "I'm brilliant at hiding."

Rainbow poked his whole head out. He looked one way. He looked the other. And he answered, in a whisper:

"All right. But just a little bit."

"I'll hide, you count to ten," said Lolo.

Rainbow counted. One, two, three… nine, ten.

And he turned round to look.

It wasn't hard at all to find him. Lolo had hidden behind a stone, very serious, very still. But the stone was small, and the octopus was big, and his eight arms were sticking out all over the place, as if the stone had hair.

Rainbow stared.

First out came a hee, hee. Then a ha, ha. And in the end, a laugh so big that it came out fizzing.

His scales lit up all at once, like fireworks under the water.

It was the first time in his life he had laughed with someone.

The laughing and the lights could be seen from far away.

First a pink starfish came over to see what was going on. Then a very elegant seahorse. Then a crab, walking sideways, and a line of silver sardines.

"Can we play?" they asked.

Rainbow felt the old fear, and he wanted to hide.

But he looked at Lolo. And Lolo winked at him.

"Of course," said Rainbow, his voice a little wobbly. "But the octopus counts first. He's terrible at hiding."

They played all morning: hide-and-seek, chase, and who could swim fastest through the seaweed.

Ever since that day, Rainbow doesn't spend his days counting alone.

He's still a little bit shy. Sometimes he still wants to hide in his coral.

But now he knows something: his colours aren't for hiding. They're for lighting up everyone else.

And when a new fish comes to the reef, one who stays very still behind a rock and doesn't dare to play, Rainbow knows exactly what to do.

He stops in front of them, without getting too close.

And he waits. The way Lolo waited.
